title: Lower Forward Barrel Skin — Flush Bonded Repair Patch for Thinned or Cracked Material
abstract: Permanent flush bonded patch for material loss or cracking in the lower forward barrel skin, applied where the remaining thickness after clean-up is below the blend limit but the damage stays inside the panel bay.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the residual fatigue capability of the lower forward barrel skin after material has been removed to clean up corrosion damage or a short crack, without adding an external step in the airflow.
sections.damage_assessment: Define the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection followed by an ultrasonic thickness map on a 25 millimetre grid. Damage that stays inside the blend limit does not need this repair and may be left blended. Damage that reaches a fastener row, that crosses a stringer, or that lies within 60 millimetres of an existing repair is outside the scope of this repair and requires an engineering assessment. Record the damage centre relative to the nearest frame and stringer before any material is removed, because the patch layout is set from that datum. Where the damage is a crack, establish both crack tips by dye penetrant before you decide the routed shape.
sections.repair_procedure: Rout the damaged material to a smooth oval with a minimum corner radius of 15 millimetres and blend the edges to a 20 to 1 ratio. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge and confirm that no indication remains. Machine the recess to the depth given on repair drawing RD-53-21-12-901 so that the patch sits flush with the surrounding skin. Prepare the bonding surfaces to the finish stated on sheet 2 and apply the chromate-free protection to all bare metal. Cut the patch from the sheet stock given on the drawing and check its fit dry. Apply the adhesive film, position the patch and cure under vacuum with the heater blanket, monitoring the skin temperature throughout. After cure, drill and install the perimeter rivets AGS534950-40 wet with sealant, working from the centre outwards. Where the repair reaches the panel clip D5321122023477, add the local packer shown on sheet 3. Restore the external finish to aerodynamic smoothness class A and re-apply the paint scheme.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 18000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a tap test of the full patch area and an ultrasonic inspection of the bond line every 5000 flight cycles. Any disbond larger than 100 square millimetres, or any new indication inside the repair boundary, makes the repair invalid and requires a new engineering assessment. Report the repair to Aeralis with the thickness map so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Material loss up to 15 per cent of the nominal skin thickness over an area not larger than 120 by 80 millimetres, not crossing a fastener row or a stringer, and not closer than 60 millimetres to an existing repair. One repair per skin bay.

issue.reason: A pre-embodiment survey is added so that a panel carrying this patch is assessed before an external bonded strap is quoted over it.
